title: Your Online Investment Advice Just Got Safer: SEBI Cracks Down on Unregulated 'Finfluencers'
description: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey recently announced new guidelines to protect investors from misleading financial advice online. These rules target 'finfluenc.

faq.a: Tuhin Kanta Pandey is the current Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), India's market regulator. He took charge on March 1, 2025.

faq.q: How can I check if a financial advisor is registered with SEBI?
faq.a: You can verify the registration status of an Investment Advisor (IA) or Research Analyst (RA) on the official SEBI website. SEBI maintains a list of all registered intermediaries.

faq.q: What kind of advice do these new rules cover?
faq.a: These rules primarily cover specific investment advice (like "buy this stock" or "invest in this mutual fund"), financial planning, and the promotion of financial products, especially when done for a fee or benefit.

faq.q: Does this apply to news channels or financial journalists?
faq.a: Generally, these rules are aimed at individuals or entities providing personalised investment advice or product recommendations for commercial gain. Reputable financial journalists and news channels typically provide general market information and analysis, not specific, personalised investment advice, and operate under different editorial guidelines.

faq.q: What should I do if an unregistered 'finfluencer' gives me bad advice?
faq.a: If you suffer losses due to advice from an unregistered 'finfluencer', your legal recourse might be limited as they are not under SEBI's direct regulatory framework. It's always best to seek advice only from SEBI-registered professionals.
